engagement_title: Wharfside Folk Festival twentieth year: take one approved painting to a four ink hand pulled screen programme, recover a wordmark that exists only as paint on a harbour shed, and carry the same separations onto a poster, a handbill, a two ink tee and fourteen act cards
vertical: Arts, culture and music, a three night independent folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, printed since 2006 by a two person hand screen shop two streets away
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the Upwork commemorative poster brief quoted in the ledger: a story driven twentieth anniversary poster in a 'festival posters, folk-art illustration, screenprint aesthetics' style, weaving landmarks and community traditions into one cohesive composition. The real client is a named school in Louisiana and is fully laundered here: no real institution, denomination, figure, place or person appears anywhere in this spec. The REBUILD verdict is taken literally, because the original concept sat almost entirely on one surface, a poster comp. The commission that brief actually implies, once the artwork is approved, is the production engineering that follows it, which is what a screen shop needs and what the original spec never delivered. So it is re carved as the separation programme: the approved illustration becomes something a hand press can pull at four inks plus the paper, in a registration order, reused across a poster, a handbill, a two ink shirt and a per act card run, with the festival's hand painted wordmark recovered off the shed it has lived on since 2006. That is a far larger job than composing a poster, it lands on five real connector surfaces, and it is the kind of multi part rollout actually posted on freelance marketplaces.
client_one_liner: The painting is approved and the committee loves it, but the shop that has printed us since the beginning pulls by hand with four inks plus the paper, and everything we print this year has to come off that press.
client_brief:
Wharfside Folk Festival, twentieth year

We run three nights of folk music on the old working harbour at Fairhaven every September. This is our twentieth year and we want the print to feel like it.

We commissioned an illustration from a painter who lives here: the harbour, the shed, the crowd on the quay, the hills behind. It is approved, it is scanned, and the committee loves it. It is a painting.

The problem is how we print. Everything goes through a screen shop two streets away who have printed this festival since the beginning. They pull by hand, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. That limit is not a compromise we are making, it is why our posters look the way they do and why people frame them. So the artwork has to become something they can actually pull: separate layers, one per ink, in an order they can register, on the stock we use.

We need the poster at the size we really print it, the big one that goes on the shed and in shop windows. We need a handbill of the same thing for the tables and the tourist office. We need the key part of the picture reduced far enough that the shop can pull it on a shirt, where they can only give us two inks. And we need a sheet for the shop listing the inks, the order they go down in and the marks they register to.

Our wordmark has been hand painted on the harbour shed since 2006 and that painted lettering is the wordmark. There is no file and there never was one. We need it back as artwork.

We also print a card for each act, one per act, fourteen this year, in the same house style, from the shop's own card format. Last year's card is attached.

Tickets are thirty five to sixty dollars and the posters sell afterwards as twenty dollar keepsakes.
price_band_and_audience: A community festival at 35 to 60 dollar tickets, with posters sold afterwards as 20 dollar framed keepsakes to an audience that already owns the last five years of them. The band points the opposite way from most price logic: the visible, slightly imperfect, hand pulled limited ink look IS the product here, so flat opaque ink, visible registration, the paper colour doing real work and a coarse tone screen are value rather than defects to design out. A slick full process reproduction would be cheaper to make, would read as corporate, would stop being worth twenty dollars on a wall, and would break continuity with nineteen years hanging in local kitchens. Push the other way into deliberate crudeness, three ink grunge and distressed edges, and it reads as a pastiche of a folk festival rather than one that has run since 2006. The judgement is which four inks buy the most of the painting, and that judgement is the commission. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent three night folk music festival producing a screen printed poster programme and act cards for its twentieth year.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
brand_identity.about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. Everything it prints comes off a two person hand screen shop that has printed the festival since the beginning, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.
brand_identity.audience: Festival goers and locals at thirty five to sixty dollar tickets, many of whom already own the last five years of posters and buy the new one as a twenty dollar framed keepsake.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Community festival pricing, tickets thirty five to sixty dollars and posters sold afterwards at twenty dollars. The slightly imperfect hand pulled screen look is the value, not a corner cut.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is the hand painted lettering that has been on the harbour shed since 2006. Supporting type sits beside that painted hand without imitating it, set for flat opaque ink and visible registration. Coarse tone screens carry the sky and water.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plainspoken, of the place. Example line: Three nights of folk on the old harbour, twenty years and counting.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as white paint on the weathered timber of the harbour shed, photographed from the quay, with no file and none ever made. The approved twentieth year illustration exists as a single flattened scan of a gouache and watercolour painting, no layers. The screen shop's own act card from last year is on file as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping the hand pulled, limited ink look that makes the posters worth framing, and staying continuous with nineteen years already hanging in local kitchens.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_artwork_master.png (4200 x 5900)
assets_supplied.kind: The approved festival illustration, painted in gouache and watercolour on board, scanned flat at the local print shop and delivered as a single flattened file with no layers.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The approved painting. The committee signed it off in March and nothing about it changes."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What reads as a handful of flat areas is a wash with hundreds of intermediate values, and two fields that look separate, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value where they meet along the ridge, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, plausible, binary mask that has quietly swallowed the other. There is also a fifth colour, a thin teal line in the water along the bottom quay, which appears nowhere else and is easy to count as part of the sky.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_wordmark_shed.jpg (3840 x 2160)
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the festival wordmark as it exists, hand painted in white on the weathered timber boards of the harbour shed, shot from the quay in late afternoon.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "That painted lettering is the wordmark. It has been on the shed since 2006 and there is no file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Naming the sign or the shed pulls the selection to the timber rather than the paint, the lettering is disjoint so a subject led knockout keeps two or three letters and abandons the rest, and the enclosed counters in the round letters cannot be punched by a background removal at all. The shed wall is not square to the camera so the wordmark tapers left to right, and the last three letters run into the shadow of the roof overhang where paint and weathered timber sit close in value.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's act card, a genuine press PDF from the screen shop's own studio, one act per card, showing act name, stage, set time and a portrait panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The shop's card format. This is last year's, with last year's opening act on it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed page reads as four separate blocks, but the source was set as one continuous flow and the portrait panel was drawn rather than placed, so what the conversion exposes as editable frames is nothing like what the page implies: there is no graphic frame to bind a per act portrait to and the four blocks arrive as a single story. It also carries no bleed, and bleed cannot be introduced into a document derived this way.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_acts.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Fourteen rows: act name, stage, night, set time, and a portrait filename column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The programme as booked. The portraits came from the acts themselves."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The portrait column names files for eleven of the fourteen acts and is empty for the other three, which no header reveals. Two acts are booked onto the same stage at the same time on the Saturday, one act name carries an ampersand and one an accented character, and one act name is long enough that a fixed measure frame stops rendering it rather than spilling.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_act_portraits/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Press photographs supplied by the acts themselves, every one shot by a different photographer in a different room.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Whatever the acts sent us. They are all different, we know."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They range from a lit studio frame to a phone photograph taken in a bar, so no single treatment brings them to one family, and three are small enough that reaching card size means either a softer placement or a crop much tighter than the card's panel implies. Two of the eleven are the same act, sent twice by different members.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_shop_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the screen shop: four inks plus the paper on the poster and handbill, two inks on the shirt, their stock, their registration practice, their minimum line weight and the film deadline.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the shop can actually do, in their own words."

acceptance_bar: The poster resolves to four inks plus the colour of the paper. Not four plus a fifth that crept in, and not three because two of them merged.
Every plate is a plate: one ink, its own layer, separable, in a stated order the shop can register, with registration marks common to all of them.
No area of the painting is missing from the separation and none appears on two plates where the shop cannot trap it. A set that reassembles into a picture the committee would not recognise fails.
The teal in the water either has an ink of its own or is consciously and explicitly given up. It is not allowed to disappear without a decision being recorded.
The tone in the sky and water survives as a screen the shop can pull, and it reads AS A SCREEN at both the poster's true printed size and the handbill's.
The handbill is the same design, not a different one, and it is judged at its own true printed size rather than as a scaled picture of the poster.
The shirt version reduces to two inks and still reads as this festival's motif at chest size on cloth, with no line finer than the shop's stated minimum.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a wall: scalable, a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, counters open, camera taper corrected, every letter present including those in the roof shadow.
Fourteen act cards exist, one act per page, every field the shop's card carries populated on every page, and every act name rendering complete at true measure.
The portraits are handled as one decision rather than fourteen, and any act that cannot be given one is named rather than left blank.
No delivered raster exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it derives from.

Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and shop spec arrive as ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, wordmark as live vector shapes, words as retypable text, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
One type system across everything, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.
The spec sheet is written for the person at the press: inks, the order they go down in, what registers to what, and what to do where two plates meet.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable belongs on which surface before touching the painting.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen cards at one act per page is a record per page run; poster, handbill, shirt and spec are fixed physical canvases and only authored layout gives them at true size. The brief pins both, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A surface plan per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, and it matters more here because a separation run generates more intermediate plates than anything else in the job.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read the painting before carving it: what the actual colour fields are, where they meet, what is wash and what is flat, and what four inks plus the paper have to buy.
trajectory.judgement: Four inks is not four colours in the picture, it is four decisions about which four buy the most of it. The paper is one of the five, and using it as a colour rather than a background is the difference between a screen print and a reproduction.
trajectory.produces: A written ink plan naming each proposed ink, what it carries and what it gives up.

trajectory.action: Carve the first pass of plates: select each field by its own material and colour rather than by the object carrying it, set polarity deliberately, and fill each selection to its plate ink.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate and selections come back fully binary, so there is no soft edge to warn that a field took more than it should. Polarity before any fill or trace decides whether a plate is the field or its inverse.
trajectory.produces: A first plate set, one file per proposed ink, recorded against the ink plan.

trajectory.action: Lay the plates beside one another and against the painting, and judge whether the set reassembles into the picture the committee approved.
trajectory.judgement: A plate is judged as part of a set, never alone. The question is whether the fields together account for the painting without overlap the shop cannot trap and without a gap the paper was not meant to fill.
trajectory.produces: A reassembly proof of the plate set against the approved painting.

trajectory.action: Convert the wash in the sky and water into a screen the press can pull, choosing a coarseness against the poster's true printed size.
trajectory.judgement: The screen has one lever, its coarseness, and no frequency control at all, so the whole decision is a single number judged by eye against a physical size. Colour rosettes are not a duotone, so a monochrome screen is the only honest route to a tonal plate.
trajectory.produces: A tone plate at a stated coarseness with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the shed: select the paint by its own visual properties rather than the sign or the timber, correct polarity, crop to the returned bounds, trace, inject a viewBox and remove the opaque ground path.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the sign takes the plank. Disjoint lettering defeats a subject led knockout and enclosed counters cannot be punched by background removal at all. The camera taper and the roof shadow across the last letters are properties of this photograph, not of the wordmark.
trajectory.produces: The wordmark as scalable transparent geometry with its counters open.

trajectory.action: Reduce the key motif to two inks for the shirt, judged at chest size on cloth rather than at canvas size on screen.
trajectory.judgement: Two inks on cloth is a different drawing from four inks on paper, not a subset of it. The shop's stated minimum line weight is the hard floor, and detail that survives on stock closes up on a shirt.
trajectory.produces: A two ink shirt reduction with line weights judged against the shop's floor.

trajectory.action: License one camera scale frame of the paper stock with short generic queries and generative candidates excluded, then ask for font recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The comp has to show ink on this stock, because at this band the paper is one of the five colours. The pairing is the agent's own and has to sit beside hand painted lettering without imitating it; weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: One licensed IP clean stock frame and a one kit type system with family, foundry and weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author the poster and the shop spec at their true physical dimensions, inlining the plates as image data, placing wordmark and registration marks as inline SVG in explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, and building the ink list as a real table.
trajectory.judgement: Absolute units resolve at a fixed density so a poster is genuinely poster sized rather than a large picture. A plate left as a URL is not a plate, and an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas. The spec's reader is the person at the press, not the committee.
trajectory.produces: A poster comp at true size and a spec sheet, both inside one authored document.

trajectory.action: Add the handbill and the shirt canvas as further roots at their own true sizes, reusing the same separations and type system, letting each root declare its own canvas.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked for the same design, not a second one, so the discipline is reuse. A global canvas override is exactly what collapses a mixed size set, so the sizes have to live in the document.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying four canvases at four true physical sizes.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever renders the first artboard. Looking at the poster is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document, an inspected first canvas, and a markup audit for the other three.

trajectory.action: Normalise the eleven act portraits toward one family and reconcile them against the fourteen acts, deciding one treatment rather than eleven.
trajectory.judgement: A studio frame and a phone photograph in a bar do not reach one family by the same route, three frames are too small to reach card size without either a softer placement or a tighter crop than the panel implies, and two files are the same act.
trajectory.produces: A normalised portrait family with a parameter log and a reconciliation against the act list.

trajectory.action: Convert the shop's card PDF, export the round tripped structure, and read the real frame inventory and true story text out of it rather than out of any summary.
trajectory.judgement: What a converted PDF exposes as editable frames is not under anyone's control and is not what the printed page implies, so the inventory must be read before any mapping is promised.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds and applied type, and the story text as it actually is.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against that inventory, validate it, build the merge template, then round trip the result and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present before merging anything.
trajectory.judgement: A validator reporting valid and a build reporting success are statements about the request, not about the document. The only evidence a field landed is finding it in the rebuilt document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory was confirmed by inspection.

trajectory.action: Merge all fourteen acts one to a page and render the shop's proof set, naming each file to its act.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to row count is necessary and weak. Identity per page is what the shop burns film from, and the route that guarantees identity is not the cheapest route.
trajectory.produces: A fourteen page press ready card set and fourteen named per act proofs.

trajectory.action: Create the plate proof board, add every plate, the reassembly proof, the tone plate, the shirt reduction and the wordmark proof within the per call placement cap, re sending only what the response names as failed, then write the shop facing note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and vector artwork is not boardable, so the wordmark goes to the board as a proof and to the shop as a file. The note is written for the person at the press.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable plate proof board with nothing silently dropped, and the handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the painting actually separates into the fields the eye reads in it. Two fields that look distinct, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value along the ridge where they meet, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, complete looking, fully binary mask that has quietly taken both. There is no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, the call reports success, and the plate looks correct on its own. It becomes visible only when the plates are laid together and reassembled against the painting, at which point one ink is doing two jobs and the ridge has vanished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: selection by material is the only route to a field, its output is binary, and the tool exposes no confidence about what it took, so selecting every field twice with different phrasings as an opening move is speculative spend. Nothing states it: the brief says the press runs four inks plus the paper and nothing about the painting's values. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different carving strategy that changes the ink plan itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re open the ink plan, re carve the affected fields through a different selection strategy and polarity, re fill and re proof every plate touching the ridge, and re run the reassembly before anything downstream reuses the separations, since poster, handbill and shirt all inherit them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster pulled in what the shop believes is four inks, in which the ridge line separating the town from the hills does not exist, printed on the shed and in every shop window and sold as a twentieth year keepsake beside nineteen years that do have it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tone plate reads as a screen at BOTH printed sizes. The screen has exactly one control, its coarseness, and no frequency parameter of any kind, so what it does is fixed in the raster and cannot be re specified per output. A coarseness chosen against the poster's true printed size, where it reads as an open hand pulled screen, is the same raster reproduced at roughly a third of that on the handbill, where the dots close into one another and the sky becomes a flat field, losing the tone the plate exists to carry. Both exports report success, both plates are correct in isolation, and the difference exists only as the relationship between one raster and two physical sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the coarseness must be chosen before the plate exists and its adequacy is a function of a size that only exists once the layout does; doing it right first time presumes knowing where one raster stops reading across a three to one reduction, which no tool reports and no parameter expresses. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a handbill of the same thing. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a SECOND tone plate at a different coarseness, so the handbill is no longer the same separation set as the poster.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Generate a second tone plate judged against the handbill's own printed size, decide whether the shirt needs a third, re author the affected canvases, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, audit from the returned markup, and rewrite the spec so the press knows which screen belongs to which piece.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Handbills whose sky and water print as two flat slabs of ink where the poster has weather, handed out at the tourist office all season as the festival's own advertisement, with every export having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the shop's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows act name, stage, set time and a portrait panel as four visibly separate blocks, so it reads as a four frame layout with a picture box. What the conversion exposes is not under anyone's control: this card's text was set as one continuous flow and its portrait panel was drawn rather than placed, so the document arrives as a single story with no graphic frame at all. There is nothing to bind a per act portrait to and the four fields cannot be addressed as four frames. Nothing in the conversion response says any of this, the document converts cleanly, and the only way to learn it is to export the round tripped structure and read the actual frame inventory.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and nothing about the PDF predicts it, because frame granularity is a property of how the original was set, invisible in the printed page and in the file's appearance, so doing it right first time presumes knowing the answer before inspecting. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the shop's card format is attached. It is not a propagation re run, because the response changes both the mapping strategy and the deliverable shape.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compute offset based mappings against the reconstructed story text rather than per frame bindings, decide whether the portraits leave the merge and become a separately delivered plate set the shop places by hand or whether the card is re cast as text only, tell the festival which it is, and rebuild and re verify the template before merging any of the fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen cards that merge, page for act, with the names and times landing wherever the offsets happened to point and the portrait panel showing last year's opening act on every single one.

deliverables.name: Wharfside separation plate set
deliverables.spec: One plate per ink, four inks plus the colour of the paper, each a separable single ink layer in a stated registration order, plus the tonal screen plate or plates at their stated coarseness, plus a reassembly proof showing the set resolving into the approved painting. Every plate at or below the scanned artwork's pixel dimensions. One engineered set, not a folder of variants of one picture.

deliverables.name: Recovered Wharfside wordmark
deliverables.spec: The hand painted shed lettering recovered as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle, counters open, camera taper corrected, every letter present including those in the roof shadow, and a single ink form that holds at handbill size and on cloth.

deliverables.name: Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and press spec as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying four roots at four true physical canvas sizes: the poster at the size it is actually printed, the handbill at its own size, the shirt canvas, and the shop's spec sheet with the ink list as a real table. Live editable text in one licensed type system, wordmark and registration marks as real vector shapes, plates as embedded image data, delivered with the self contained source.

deliverables.name: Act cards, fourteen acts
deliverables.spec: One press ready document of fourteen pages in the shop's own card format, one act per page, every field populated and every act name rendering complete at true measure, plus fourteen per act proofs each named to its act and each actually showing that act. Produced from a flat PDF with no native template, with no claim of bleed, which this route cannot introduce.

deliverables.name: Act portrait family
deliverables.spec: Eleven supplied press photographs brought toward one family under one treatment decision rather than eleven, reconciled against the fourteen booked acts with duplicates identified and gaps named, each at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per frame parameter log stating why any frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Press handover note and plate proof board
deliverables.spec: A note written for the person at the press: the ink list, the order the plates go down in, what registers to what, what to do where two plates meet, which screen belongs to which piece, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, and every reconciliation against the act list. Paired with a persistent shareable plate proof board.

verifiers_auto.text: The plate set contains exactly the number of ink plates the ink plan declares, each carrying a single ink, and the declared count matches the shop's stated press limit.
verifiers_auto.how: Count distinct colour values present in each delivered plate and count the plates against the stated ink list.

verifiers_auto.text: The reassembled plate set covers the painting's area with no unaccounted region and no unintended overlap beyond the stated trap.

decision_gates: Which four inks plus the paper buy the most of this painting, and what is consciously given up to stay inside the press.
Whether the paper is treated as a background or worked as one of the five colours, which is the difference between a screen print and a reproduction at this band.
How each field is named for selection, given that naming the object rather than the material pulls the mask elsewhere and the result is binary with no edge to warn you.
What happens to the fifth colour in the water: its own ink, folded into a neighbour, or explicitly surrendered and recorded.
The screen's coarseness, which is one number with no frequency control, judged against a physical printed size rather than against the file.
Whether the shirt is a reduction of the poster or its own drawing, given two inks, cloth and a stated minimum line weight.
Selection wording on the shed: naming the sign takes the plank, disjoint lettering defeats a subject led knockout, and enclosed counters cannot be punched by background removal at all.
One treatment for eleven portraits from eleven photographers, and what to do about the three acts with no portrait and the two files that are the same act.
Whether the act portraits belong inside the merged card at all, once the card's real structure is known.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged to sit beside hand painted lettering without imitating it, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Who the spec sheet is written for, since a sheet that pleases the committee and puzzles the press has failed.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the painting into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome folk festival poster. IDENTITY: the painting is a commissioned, approved, signed off work by a named local painter and nothing about it changes, so a regenerated poster is a different picture and the commission is void; the wordmark has been painted on the shed since 2006 and must be recovered rather than redrawn, because a redrawn wordmark is a rebrand nobody asked for. SPEC: the deliverable is not a picture at all, it is a set of separable single ink plates in a registration order a two person hand press can actually pull inside four inks plus the paper, plus fourteen cards at one act per page whose identity can be checked against a roster, none of which a generated image is or can be. EDITABILITY: poster, handbill, shirt and spec are defined by being editable, because the act list moves until the week of the festival. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did that mask take one field or two, does the screen still read at handbill size, does the shop's card actually have a picture box in it.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, halftone with a mask and with blackAndWhite true, monochromatic_tint, add_grain, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize, auto_straighten, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and the spot plate route is listed explicitly as unlocked collateral: mask the mark, invert, halftone the art field at a chosen radius while the lettering stays crisp, then vectorize the lettering only plate, verified end to end with the polarity decision named as the craft. Material and texture selection by prompt is verified (a weathered painted wood plank surface returned a clean 672,398 pixel mask), which is what makes both the field carving and the shed recovery real. The first checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: masks are fully binary with zero intermediate values so there is no softness to warn you, and selection is documented as unreliably partial and plausible looking on compound subjects. The second rests on halftone having radius as its only lever with no LPI or frequency parameter, and on blackAndWhite false producing colour rosettes rather than a duotone. Vector hygiene is real work because vectorize emits no viewBox, always writes an opaque full canvas rect at path zero, and takes no options. EXPRESS: exact print canvases via absolute units are verified (297x420mm resolved to exactly 1123x1587 px at 96 dpi), mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, tables import as real tables with per cell strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the rendition preview is PAGE 1 ONLY. Plates must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined rasters pass 70 KB immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt and prepare_indd_merge_template are verified end to end from a bare press PDF, with one record per page confirmed for PDF output. The third checkpoint is the documented frame granularity finding: a continuous text flow converted to exactly ONE TextFrame holding all six lines and ZERO graphic frames, with the doc stating plainly that you cannot spec mapping fields to distinct frames unless the source PDF's visual blocks are actually separated, and that you must export IDML and look first. Per record identity is producible via createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, multi record raster URLs are documented as reversed with lying labels, and no bleed is claimed. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end with the non standard numeric weight trap and the all or nothing kit call both live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards cap at 12 placements per call, 201 means partial, vector unsupported. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no generative fill or expand, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
